articles.title: The Hubble Space Telescope Anniversary - 25 YEARS
articles.summary: This article celebrates the 25th anniversary of the Hubble Space Telescope, highlighting its profound impact on astronomy since its launch in 1990. It details how Hubble, named after Edwin Hubble, built upon Galileo's legacy by providing an unobstructed view of the universe from space, leading to revolutionary discoveries about the age and size of the universe, stellar life cycles, exoplanets, black holes, and the formation of stars and galaxies. The telescope's observations have fundamentally reshaped humanity's understanding of the cosmos.

articles.title: NASA Pluto Probe Begins Search for New Moons, Ring
articles.summary: NASA's New Horizons probe, nearing its historic July 14 flyby of Pluto, has begun actively searching for previously undiscovered moons and rings. This search aims to identify any potential hazards that could impact the spacecraft during its close encounter with the dwarf planet system, which is currently known to have five moons.

articles.title: SJAA Member Observation Reports
articles.summary: This article compiles several observation reports from SJAA members, detailing diverse astronomical experiences. Members describe the awe of observing Saturn, recount a celestial-themed hike and binocular observations in Death Valley National Park, and document two ambitious attempts to replicate William Herschel's legendary deep-sky galaxy sweep. The collection also includes a report on extensive deep-sky galaxy hunting during a multi-night camping trip to Tuttle Creek under dark skies.

articles.title: Moon Eclipse Photography Tips
articles.summary: This article provides practical tips for photographing a moon eclipse, emphasizing that no specialized equipment is required and even cell phones can capture good images. It offers guidance on camera settings like ISO and exposure, focusing techniques, and general advice for both beginners and DSLR users to capture the event effectively while still enjoying the view. The author stresses the importance of pre-planning settings and encourages simplicity over excessive shooting.

articles.title: SOLAR TRANSITIONS OF THE STELLAR KIND
articles.summary: This article announces a leadership transition within the SJAA Solar Program, with Bill O'Neil taking over from Michael Packer in May 2015. Michael Packer successfully led the program for over three years, establishing "Solar Sundays" and acquiring a Lunt H-alpha telescope. Bill O'Neil, an experienced astronomy volunteer, aims to expand solar education and outreach opportunities for the SJAA.

articles.title: Solar Sunday March 1st In Honor of Leonard Nimoy
articles.summary: On March 1st, a "Solar Sunday" event gathered about 15 visitors to observe the sun, reporting 53 sunspots, 11 filaments, and limb prominences, along with a C-Class flare. The event also served as a tribute to Leonard Nimoy, acknowledging Star Trek's influence on amateur astronomy and the shared spirit of exploration. Participants discussed Nimoy's legacy and how Spock's character embodies the ideals of seeking out and exploring the universe.

articles.title: SJAA MEMBERS ATTEND GOOGLE STAR PARTY
articles.summary: On February 10, 2015, Google hosted a large Star Party for over 800 employees, family, and friends at Garfield Park, featuring over 40 telescopes supported by numerous Bay Area astronomy clubs, including SJAA. The event also included interactive booths and a significant announcement: Google's $1 Million donation to Lick Observatory. The star party received rave reviews for its engaging activities and the opportunity for attendees to observe celestial objects.

articles.title: Annual SJAA Auction Sunday, March 8, 2015
articles.summary: The article recaps the San Jose Astronomical Association's (SJAA) 35th Annual Spring Auction held on March 8, 2015, highlighting its history from a modest start to a well-organized event. It thanks volunteers and organizers for their efforts, noting improvements in managing the 156 items over the years. The auction was a success, with SJAA selling $3,749 worth of items and individual sellers bringing in $4,887.

articles.title: Did You Know?
articles.summary: This "Did You Know?" article, sourced from Astronomy Magazine's March 2015 issue, presents a collection of intriguing astronomical facts. It covers topics such as the exact number of constellations, Ganymede's volume relative to Mercury's, the closest star to the Sun, the prevalence of craters on the Moon, and scientific discoveries like plate tectonics on Europa and a subsurface ocean on Enceladus. The piece serves as an informational compilation of general astronomy trivia.

articles.title: Club Updates
articles.summary: The article outlines various programs and resources offered by the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) for its members and the wider community. These include a dedicated library, free telescope repair and tune-up sessions, monthly solar observing events, educational programs like Quick STARt and Intro to the Night Sky, and an equipment loaner program. The SJAA also hosts school star parties and provides key contact information for club activities and leadership.

articles.title: SJAA Board Updates and Meeting Excerpts
articles.summary: This document provides updates from the SJAA Board of Directors, including newly elected officers and upcoming events like Pinnacles, GSSP, and Cal Star. It also details excerpts from the March, April, and May 2015 board meetings, covering topics such as club goals (documentation, procedures), asset divestment, establishing a Meetup group, securing internet at Houge Park, and approving budgets for publicity and a new loaner equipment program. Decisions were made regarding event planning, membership engagement, and operational improvements for the club.
